name: Townview Phase I (Townview Apartments Redevelopment Phase 1)
award: 2025 Federal 4% and noncompetitive state housing tax credits
headline: Rocky Mountain Communities plans Townview Phase I, 160 new apartments and townhomes for households at 40% to 80% AMI on the block at 1600 Hooker Street in West Colfax, the first of four phases replacing its 1963 Townview community near Empower Field. It won a 2025 federal 4% award with noncompetitive state and TOC credits from CHFA, backed by City and County of Denver bonds.
why_it_matters: A nonprofit is rebuilding its own 1960s affordable property at higher density, whose existing affordability restrictions run only through 2028, with layered state money (a $3.5M Prop 123 loan and a Division of Housing award); the Denver bond inducement has not yet reached City Council, so that is the next gate.

status.label: Credits awarded; construction expected to start Q2 2027 (sponsor); bonds not yet before Denver City Council
status.detail: RMC's 2025 annual report (April 2026) gives an approximate construction start in Q2 2027 and completion in Q2 2029. A new partnership, Townview Redevelopment I LLLP, was registered in March 2026. No Denver inducement resolution or bond ordinance for Townview was found in Council records through October 2026, and the city's July 2026 bond briefing named other projects as upcoming. No closing, permit or demolition record was found.

next_step: Watch for a Denver City Council inducement resolution and bond ordinance for up to $27.4M of Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds, then site plan and demolition permits for the 1600 Hooker block.

background.text: RMC bought Townview in 1997 with affordability requirements that run through 2028, and told NeighborWorks Capital in 2023 it planned up to 400 new apartments on the site.

The owner applied on 2023-04-18 to rezone the 1600 block so it could build a 5-story permanently affordable development. The June 2023 Planning Board staff report reviewed G-MU-5; by the September 2023 Council hearing the request was G-RX-5, which Council passed on 2023-09-25 after postponing the 2023-09-11 hearing at the applicant's request.

BusinessDen reported in April 2025 a four-phase plan over about 4.5 acres along 17th Avenue and Grove and Hooker Streets, demolishing the existing buildings over about six years to build about 450 income-restricted units.

RMC describes the redevelopment as four phases serving workers who might otherwise be displaced, with on-site management and resident services. The state says the developers intend the units to help offset the loss of affordable housing in surrounding neighborhoods.

An April 2025 Naked Denver post described a proposed 6-story, 153-unit, 100% income-restricted building (40-80% AMI) at 1650 Hooker Street on the western half of a split parcel, with 109 structured parking spaces and a 3,200 sq ft commercial bay; it did not name the developer, so its link to Townview Phase I is inferred, not confirmed.
Denver's July 2026 private activity bond briefing named only Link and Pin and Green Valley Vistas as upcoming bond projects; Townview was not listed.
No public record found of Section 8 project-based vouchers; CHFA marks the Section 8 column No.
